title: How does a proposal acquire the force of federal law?

nodes.label: What kind of congressional action is proposed?
nodes.detail: A bill that changes legal rights ordinarily needs bicameral passage and presentment. Identify the action’s legal effect before selecting a procedure.

nodes.label: Draft and refer the proposal
nodes.detail: Legislative counsel, members, committee staff and outside participants can contribute. Referral and committee work explain why committee materials often provide context for specialized provisions.

nodes.label: Has the proposal reached the floor?
nodes.detail: Hearings, markup and committee reports can shape a bill. Chamber procedures can permit other routes to floor consideration.

nodes.label: Did both chambers pass the same text?
nodes.detail: Each chamber must agree to one text. A conference or another exchange of amendments can resolve differences.

nodes.label: What happened on presentment?
nodes.detail: Present the bill to the President. Signature or a two-thirds override in each chamber can enact it. Article I separately governs presidential inaction, including when adjournment prevents return.

nodes.label: Does Congress seek to alter legal consequences?
nodes.detail: Chadha invalidated a one-house resolution reversing an individual immigration decision. Congress can oversee execution or pursue new legislation through Article I.

nodes.label: Federal law enacted
nodes.detail: Begin with the enacted text and the applicable effective-date provisions. Earlier versions and reports can help identify how wording evolved.

nodes.label: No new law on this path
nodes.detail: A draft, one-chamber passage or an unoverridden veto cannot itself supply the authority the proposed text would grant.

nodes.label: Existing law still governs execution
nodes.detail: Oversight can inform a future bill. Evaluate any effort to direct execution under the separate Article II and separation-of-powers rules.

nodes.label: Did Congress adopt a budget resolution with reconciliation instructions?
nodes.detail: Class 2, slides 11–12. The concurrent resolution is an internal congressional decision. It can direct committees to propose changes to spending, revenue or the debt limit. It receives no presidential signature and changes no statute by itself.

links.label: CRS, The Reconciliation Process: Frequently Asked Questions

edges.label: Instructed committees produce a reconciliation bill

nodes.label: Consider the committees’ proposed statutory changes
nodes.detail: When multiple committees respond, the Budget Committee packages their proposals. The statutory limit on Senate debate permits a vote without cloture. The Byrd rule restricts extraneous provisions. Each chamber must agree to identical bill text before presentment.

nodes.label: Congress set budget terms; existing statutes still govern
nodes.detail: A budget resolution alone grants no new spending authority and does not amend spending, revenue or debt-limit law. Those changes require legislation.

title: How would a textualist and a purposivist read the same statute?

nodes.label: What language is disputed?
nodes.detail: Use Holy Trinity’s prohibition on importing a person under contract to perform labor or service. The church contracted with a rector. The question was whether the statutory prohibition reached that arrangement.

edges.label: Compare opinions in a second case

nodes.label: Read the enacted words in context
nodes.detail: Ask how an informed reader in the relevant period would understand labor or service, the statute’s exceptions and the surrounding provisions. An express exception can show Congress knew how to narrow coverage.

nodes.label: Identify the problem Congress addressed
nodes.detail: The Holy Trinity Court examined the statute’s title, the social problem and legislative materials. It treated the imported labor Congress targeted as distinct from employing a minister.

nodes.label: How broad is the postal exception?
nodes.detail: In Dolan, the majority read loss and miscarriage to illuminate negligent transmission. The dissent read the transmission language more broadly and gave weight to sovereign immunity.

nodes.label: Apply broader coverage if the reading holds
nodes.detail: A textualist argument could apply the labor statute to the rector. Identify why the surrounding law supports the broader reading and confront any anomaly directly.

nodes.label: Apply the narrower construction
nodes.detail: Holy Trinity held the rector outside the prohibition. A separate textual argument would need to justify that result through enacted language and context.

nodes.label: Dolan majority allows the tort claim to proceed
nodes.detail: The alleged injury came from mail left on a porch. The exception protects against specified failures to transmit mail and did not bar that slip-and-fall claim.

nodes.label: Dolan dissent would apply the exception
nodes.detail: The dissent would give the phrase a broader reach over injuries arising from negligent transmission. The majority’s narrower construction controlled the judgment.

title: Which legislative history supports the proposed reading?

nodes.label: Where does the document sit in lawmaking?
nodes.detail: Record when the document appeared, who produced it and which text it addresses. A statement concerning a discarded draft may answer a different question.

nodes.label: Does the report describe the enacted provision?
nodes.detail: Committee reports can reflect delegated drafting work. A conference explanation may illuminate the compromise that both chambers received. Compare the exact provisions and dates.

nodes.label: Who spoke, when and to whom?
nodes.detail: A sponsor explaining a negotiated clause to a voting chamber can supply context. A single member’s aspiration or a strategic insertion carries less evidence of shared understanding.

nodes.label: Was the explanation made after enactment?
nodes.detail: Later lawmakers or commentators can offer historical context or recommend reform. Determine whether they can point to contemporaneous evidence.

nodes.label: Does the record support the disputed inference?
nodes.detail: Holy Trinity used purpose-oriented evidence to read labor or service narrowly. Katzmann’s approach asks whether publicly available materials illuminate the enacted provision’s operation.

nodes.label: Use the document as interpretive evidence
nodes.detail: State the inference and its source precisely. Under a textualist approach, treat legislative history’s force separately from public linguistic and statutory context.

nodes.label: Give the document limited weight
nodes.detail: Rely on the enacted language and stronger contemporaneous evidence. Explain whether the source reflects an earlier proposal, a lone view or a later assessment.

title: Which interpretive canon fits the textual problem?

nodes.label: What textual feature creates the dispute?
nodes.detail: Canons give reasons to prefer one reading. Identify the feature before comparing the resulting reading with the whole statute.

nodes.label: Is the disputed word inside a list or after examples?
nodes.detail: Noscitur reads a word with its associates. Ejusdem asks whether a catchall following examples is confined to their shared class. Identify the class using actual text.

nodes.label: Compare the ordinary reading with the neighbors
nodes.detail: Gustafson read prospectus in its statutory company. Dolan used loss and miscarriage to inform the scope of negligent transmission.

nodes.label: Identify the common trait of the examples
nodes.detail: McBoyle read any other self-propelled vehicle against enumerated land vehicles and fair warning. Test whether the examples suggest the category advanced by each side.

nodes.label: Does this domain use an established term of art?
nodes.detail: Compare legal usage, ordinary usage and enacted definitions. Arlington Central examined whether costs conveyed notice of responsibility for expert fees.

nodes.label: Does the interpretation create surplusage or an anomaly?
nodes.detail: Test overlapping provisions together. Riggs supplies an anomalous-result example and a dissent emphasizing statutory text and institutional limits.

nodes.label: Does the canon fit the statute as a whole?
nodes.detail: Compare definitions, exceptions, parallel terms and purpose evident in the scheme. Identify a stronger counter-reading where a different canon points the other way.

nodes.label: Use the canon to support the reading
nodes.detail: Specify the feature and the inference. Explain why the statute’s context supports the resulting scope.

nodes.label: Limit the canon’s force
nodes.detail: Read the entire provision and explain which contextual evidence weakens the inference the canon would otherwise support.

title: When does a presumption change the reading?

nodes.label: Which background presumption is relevant?
nodes.detail: Identify the kind of statute and the institutional reason for demanding clarity. Each presumption addresses a particular legal consequence.

nodes.label: Does serious ambiguity persist after interpretation?
nodes.detail: McBoyle’s reading of vehicle emphasized fair warning. Apply ordinary tools first and check the jurisdiction’s formulation of when lenity operates.

nodes.label: Did the recipient get clear notice of the condition?
nodes.detail: Arlington Central asked whether a state accepting IDEA funds would clearly understand that it could owe expert fees. The Court held that the provision gave insufficient notice.

nodes.label: Is the dispute foreign conduct or a foreign legal predicate?
nodes.detail: Small construed any court to exclude foreign convictions in the provision at issue. Compare the Second Circuit’s Gayle analysis and examine the full statutory context for contrary indications.

nodes.label: Has Congress waived immunity for this claim?
nodes.detail: Identify the federal waiver and its exceptions. In Dolan, the disputed issue was the scope of the postal exception to an existing FTCA waiver.

nodes.label: Apply the supported statutory coverage
nodes.detail: State which language and context establish coverage or overcome the presumption. A presumption about immunity, notice or domestic scope answers the question specific to its domain.

nodes.label: Apply the narrower result for this presumption
nodes.detail: The consequence may be narrower criminal liability, an unenforceable funding condition, a domestic-only reading or immunity. Tie the result to the statute and the presumption actually triggered.

title: How can two apparently conflicting statutes coexist?

nodes.label: What exactly overlaps?
nodes.detail: Identify each statute’s legal command, its protected activity and the same conduct allegedly governed by both. In Epic Systems, the FAA’s arbitration command and NLRA § 7 were the claimed source of conflict.

nodes.label: Can both statutes operate as construed?
nodes.detail: Epic’s majority treated NLRA § 7 as protecting organizing and collective bargaining without displacing individual arbitration procedures. The dissent read concerted activity to encompass collective litigation.

nodes.label: What kind of arbitration defense is asserted?
nodes.detail: The FAA saving clause preserves generally applicable contract defenses. Epic held that the attack on individualized proceedings targeted a fundamental attribute of the arbitration agreements at issue.

nodes.label: Does one provision address the conflict specifically?
nodes.detail: Read the actual limits of the more specific rule and the remainder of the general rule. A tailored construction can leave meaningful work for both.

nodes.label: Is congressional displacement clearly established?
nodes.detail: Implied repeals are disfavored. Look for clear congressional intent or genuinely irreconcilable commands before concluding the earlier rule yields within the overlap.

nodes.label: Give effect to both provisions
nodes.detail: Epic applied the FAA to enforce the agreements as written. Apply the other statute to the sphere in which its commands continue to operate.

nodes.label: Resolve the defense under the saving clause framework
nodes.detail: A generally applicable formation or avoidance defense calls for its own merits and FAA preemption analysis.

nodes.label: Limit displacement to the demonstrated conflict
nodes.detail: Identify the scope of the later or more specific rule and preserve the rest of both enactments as far as their text allows.

title: Did Congress lawfully delegate this choice?

nodes.label: What choice did Congress leave open?
nodes.detail: Identify the enabling provision, the actor, the people affected and the actual discretion. Check scope and breadth together.

nodes.label: Did Congress specify the policy and consequence?
nodes.detail: Brig Aurora and Field distinguish a law taking effect upon a fact from an executive choice about what law ought to be.

nodes.label: Do regulations implement a defined statutory program?
nodes.detail: Grimaud sustained regulations governing use of federal forest reserves within a congressional plan. Congress supplied the penalty for violations.

nodes.label: Does the statute supply an intelligible principle?
nodes.detail: Read the statute’s goal, designated decisionmaker and boundaries. Hampton’s tariff adjustment standard and Yakus’s price-control constraints illustrate statutory guidance.

edges.label: Vague grant across a wide domain

nodes.label: Can the statutory limits be applied to this decision?
nodes.detail: Whitman upheld a health-based air-standard delegation. FCC v. Consumers’ Research in 2025 upheld statutory limits on universal-service contributions and found that the FCC retained final decision authority.

edges.label: Statutory policy and limits are workable

nodes.label: Could a fair reading supply a constitutional boundary?
nodes.detail: Compare Amalgamated Meat Cutters and Schechter’s sweeping authority to approve industry codes. Whitman says agency self-restraint cannot cure an unconstitutional grant.

nodes.label: Apply the statutory limit
nodes.detail: Specify what policy Congress made and what discretion survives the limiting construction. Review the agency’s action for conformity with that limit.

nodes.label: Delegation survives this challenge
nodes.detail: The delegate still has to stay within the statute. An action exceeding a valid grant presents a separate statutory question.

nodes.label: Delegation fails this test
nodes.detail: Identify which statutory choice lacked guidance and why its breadth matters. Schechter remains the course’s example of invalidation.

title: How would competing nondelegation theories decide the hard case?

nodes.label: Which nondelegation argument is at issue?
nodes.detail: Use Gundy’s pre-Act registration provision to test whether Congress chose coverage and delegated implementation. Identify the controlling judgment, separate opinions and alternative institutional proposals.

nodes.label: What did Congress require as a matter of construction?
nodes.detail: The Gundy plurality read SORNA to require pre-Act registration as soon as feasible. Alito concurred in the judgment under existing doctrine while expressing willingness to revisit it.

nodes.label: The Court upheld the delegation in Gundy
nodes.detail: The plurality and the concurrence supplied five votes for the judgment. Amalgamated Meat Cutters also illustrates a court identifying limits in the scheme and statutory context.

nodes.label: Who made the primary policy under the dissent’s account?
nodes.detail: Gorsuch’s Gundy dissent would permit executive fact-finding, filling details and assignments rooted in another branch’s power. It read SORNA as leaving the coverage decision itself to the Attorney General.

edges.label: Congress left coverage to the executive
Congress fixed policy and delegated details

nodes.label: The dissent would invalidate the grant
nodes.detail: The dissent considered pre-Act coverage a legislative policy decision. Read the historical arguments alongside criticism that early practice and institutional design do not yield one mechanically determinate line.

nodes.label: What feature makes the discretion accountable?
nodes.detail: Mistretta examined statutory sentencing goals, constraints and commission structure. Coglianese asks how many dimensions of discretion the statute leaves open.

edges.label: Limits or structure guide the delegate

nodes.label: Assess the implemented design
nodes.detail: Consider legal standards, scope, supervision and political accountability. Mistretta upheld the Sentencing Commission scheme against the challenges before the Court.

nodes.label: Congressional approval is a design proposal
nodes.detail: The assigned REINS discussion describes approaches requiring congressional approval of major rules. Keep that proposal separate from judicial review of asserted authority and the enacted statute at issue.

title: Can Congress control execution after enacting the statute?

nodes.label: How is Congress seeking control?
nodes.detail: Identify the actor and whether the mechanism changes legal rights, selects officers or reserves their removal. Congressional oversight can inform legislation and expose administrative choices.

nodes.label: Were bicameralism and presentment used?
nodes.detail: Chadha treated the one-house decision as legislative because it changed the rights and duties of persons outside Congress. Statutory authorization of that procedure failed to make it constitutional.

nodes.label: Will the official exercise significant federal authority?
nodes.detail: Buckley distinguished investigation and reporting in aid of Congress from execution and enforcement by federal officers.

nodes.label: Does Congress retain removal power over an executor?
nodes.detail: Bowsher treated the Comptroller General’s deficit-reduction duties as execution and held that congressional control over his removal was incompatible with those duties.

edges.label: Ordinary congressional removal of an executor
Evaluate a different Article II structure

nodes.label: Congress can change the program by law
nodes.detail: A valid statute can change the rules governing future execution. Review substantive and constitutional limits on the new program separately.

nodes.label: The mechanism violates the separation of powers
nodes.detail: Tie the defect to the mechanism used. Chadha addresses an individual legislative reversal and Bowsher addresses Congress retaining authority over an executor.

nodes.label: Apply constitutional officer rules
nodes.detail: Use the Appointments Clause for selection and Article II doctrine for tenure. Impeachment is a separately prescribed constitutional process.

nodes.label: Oversight can inform congressional work
nodes.detail: Hearings, reporting and legislative inquiry can inform appropriations or new legislation. Assess any added binding direction for its own legal effect.

title: Was this official constitutionally appointed?

nodes.label: What functions does the official actually perform?
nodes.detail: The constitutional classification depends on the office and authority, including the continuity of the position and the significance of its discretion.

nodes.label: Who directs and reviews the officer’s work?
nodes.detail: Edmond looked to direction and supervision by Senate-confirmed officers. Arthrex treated unreviewable final patent decisions as incompatible with appointment as an inferior officer under that structure.

nodes.label: Did the President appoint with Senate consent?
nodes.detail: Article II prescribes presidential nomination and appointment with Senate advice and consent for principal officers.

nodes.label: Did Congress vest appointment in a permitted actor?
nodes.detail: Congress can vest appointment in the President alone, a court of law or a department head. In Freytag, the Tax Court qualified as a court of law.

nodes.label: Are the new duties germane to the original office?
nodes.detail: Shoemaker and Weiss permit certain germane assignments without a new appointment. If the new duties create a distinct office, classify its authority and examine appointment afresh.

nodes.label: Identify relief fitted to the constitutional defect
nodes.detail: Lucia received a new hearing before a different, properly appointed adjudicator. Arthrex made review by the Director available and remanded for possible review.

nodes.label: Ordinary staff hiring rules govern
nodes.detail: An employee who lacks significant federal authority falls outside the Appointments Clause officer route. Inspect actual delegated powers if the job title obscures the role.

nodes.label: Appointment clears the identified test
nodes.detail: Check that the appointing actor and the source of appointment authority match the office classification.

title: May this official be removed, by whom and on what grounds?

nodes.label: Who wants to remove which official?
nodes.detail: Read the tenure and removal statute, identify who appointed and supervises the official, and ask who is invoking the removal power.

nodes.label: Would Congress control an officer executing the law?
nodes.detail: Bowsher bars congressional retention of removal control over such an officer outside impeachment. Myers invalidated a statutory Senate-consent condition on firing the postmaster at issue.

edges.label: Executive removal governed by a tenure limit

nodes.label: What kind of office and protection are involved?
nodes.detail: Use office function, statutory tenure and supervision. The Class 11 slides follow the Roberts Court’s 2010, 2020 and 2021 decisions. The Slaughter supplement covers the June 2026 shift. Treat the 1935 Humphrey’s FTC rule as historical.

edges.label: Single director leading an executive agency

nodes.label: Slaughter rejected FTC removal protection
nodes.detail: On June 29, 2026, the Court reversed and remanded on the merits, overruling Humphrey’s Executor and rejecting the FTC Act’s restriction on presidential removal.

nodes.label: Seila Law rejected the CFPB’s single-director protection
nodes.detail: Seila Law (2020) held the CFPB director’s for-cause protection unconstitutional and severable. Collins (2021) applied the rule to the FHFA director. For retrospective relief, Collins distinguished the removal defect from invalid appointment and required a showing of harm.

nodes.label: Test a chain with two removal protections
nodes.detail: Free Enterprise Fund (2010) invalidated the two-level for-cause protection for PCAOB members and severed the board-level protection. The particular supervision and layering mattered to the holding.

nodes.label: Compare the duties and the interference with supervision
nodes.detail: Wiener inferred protection for war-claims adjudicators and Morrison upheld the independent counsel’s good-cause protection. Slaughter expressly reserved tenure protections for judges of non–Article III courts. Check the office-specific rationale and scope.

nodes.label: Cook treated the Federal Reserve separately
nodes.detail: The Court’s June 29, 2026 stay decision left interim protection in place and addressed the Fed’s distinctive statutory and historical setting. Distinguish the stay order’s analysis from a final judgment on the facts of Cook’s removal.

nodes.label: Determine who holds the ordinary removal power
nodes.detail: Check the governing appointment and management structure and any independently applicable civil-service protections. Tenure for a fixed term alone does not answer whether the official can be removed sooner.

nodes.label: Congressional control fails for this executive function
nodes.detail: Identify the impermissible removal mechanism before determining whether the statute can continue to operate without it.

title: Can someone serve without a new Senate confirmation?

nodes.label: What authority is invoked to fill the vacancy?
nodes.detail: Distinguish a constitutional recess commission from temporary performance of duties under a federal vacancy or succession statute.

nodes.label: Is the Senate in a qualifying recess?
nodes.detail: Noel Canning covers both intersession and intrasession recesses and preexisting vacancies. The Senate’s pro forma sessions counted while it retained capacity to transact business. A recess shorter than ten days is presumptively too short, absent highly unusual circumstances.

nodes.label: Check when the commission ends
nodes.detail: Article II permits a recess commission that expires at the end of the Senate’s next session. Distinguish appointment to the office from temporary performance of its functions.

nodes.label: Does a general or special statute cover the office?
nodes.detail: The FVRA covers many Senate-confirmed offices but excludes members of certain multimember boards. Identify any office-specific succession provision and how it interacts with the FVRA.

nodes.label: Is this person eligible under that route?
nodes.detail: The FVRA generally uses the first assistant or permits qualifying presidential designations of certain Senate-confirmed or senior agency officials. Also check nomination restrictions and any separate constitutional challenge.

nodes.label: Is the official within the statutory service period?
nodes.detail: The FVRA ordinarily allows 210 days, subject to exceptions including periods linked to a nomination. Determine which duties were performed and when.

nodes.label: Temporary service can proceed
nodes.detail: Record the basis and time limit. The CFPB succession example in the course concerns preliminary relief and later dismissal of the suit.

nodes.label: This appointment or acting route fails
nodes.detail: Consider another authorized route. For a disputed agency act, examine the precise statutory consequence, including the FVRA’s rules for exclusive functions and duties where applicable.

title: How much authority does the President have for this action?

nodes.label: What does Congress say about this action?
nodes.detail: Identify the asserted action at the relevant level of specificity. Use Jackson’s Youngstown concurrence to compare the President’s own Article II authority with Congress’s position.

nodes.label: Category one. Is the action within the authorization?
nodes.detail: The President combines independent authority with the power Congress can delegate. Dames & Moore found substantial statutory support for part of the claims settlement and identified acquiescence for the rest.

edges.label: Compare a statutory claim at the stay stage

nodes.label: Trump v. Illinois tested the statute at the stay stage
nodes.detail: On December 23, 2025, the Court denied a stay after finding the government had not established that the statute authorized the claimed federalization in the circumstances presented. Its ruling concerned interim relief.

nodes.label: Category two. Does practice support the claimed authority?
nodes.detail: Examine an established practice, congressional knowledge and concurrent authority. Midwest Oil illustrates the use of longstanding practice and acquiescence. Mere silence and acquiescence can carry different weight.

nodes.label: Category three. Is the claimed power exclusive?
nodes.detail: Youngstown invalidated the steel seizure. Little v. Barreme illustrates limits on presidential departure from a statute’s terms. An incompatible measure needs an exclusive constitutional basis to prevail.

nodes.label: Is the law imposing a specific duty?
nodes.detail: Kendall allowed an order requiring performance of a ministerial duty. Identify the command and distinguish performance of that duty from a discretionary policy judgment.

nodes.label: The officer must carry out the ministerial duty
nodes.detail: The President’s supervisory position supplies no authority to disregard this specific statutory command. Identify a court’s remedial authority separately.

nodes.label: The asserted authority can support the action
nodes.detail: State the category and its precise source of authority. Verify separate statutory constraints on the way the President implements it.

nodes.label: The stated authority is insufficient
nodes.detail: In category two, identify the missing basis. In category three, explain why Congress’s inconsistent command governs.

title: How does White House regulatory review affect an agency decision?

nodes.label: What is the White House asking the agency to do?
nodes.detail: Identify the executive order, review request, return letter or substantive directive. Keep the regulated party’s legal obligations tied to final agency action.

edges.label: Urgent dispute over a statutory deadline

nodes.label: What did Congress require or authorize?
nodes.detail: Read the agency’s organic statute and its required factors. The OLC regulatory-review defense assumes oversight consistent with the agency’s statutory authority.

nodes.label: Who actually makes and explains the decision?
nodes.detail: Coordinate through the review process and identify the agency official with delegated authority. Civil-service arrangements and internal delegation can affect who supplies analysis and who signs.

nodes.label: Can review occur without violating the statutory deadline?
nodes.detail: Tyson addressed delayed OSHA standard-setting in the face of statutory deadlines and OMB review. A specific statutory deadline and a required decision retain independent legal force.

nodes.label: Does the final action give agency reasons under the statute?
nodes.detail: The final record should explain the statutory factors the agency used and the resulting choice. Check whether changes urged by White House reviewers fit the agency’s mandate.

nodes.label: The agency issues its decision
nodes.detail: The agency’s lawful final action supplies the operative decision and is reviewed in the appropriate statutory channel.

nodes.label: The record is vulnerable on judicial review
nodes.detail: Identify the factor omitted or the reason outside the statute. Review the final agency action on the rationale the agency supplied.

nodes.label: The statutory command controls the schedule
nodes.detail: Identify the act due, applicable deadline and available remedy for a legally required act that remains unperformed.

title: Rulemaking or adjudication, and what process follows?

nodes.label: Does the action prescribe a rule or decide a case?
nodes.detail: APA § 551 distinguishes making rules from issuing orders and treats licensing as adjudicative. For due process, compare Bi-Metallic’s general citywide valuation increase with Londoner’s assessment of particular properties based on individual facts.

nodes.label: Is this federal agency rulemaking?
nodes.detail: Identify the federal agency, the organic statute and any special procedure. For state or local action, consult the applicable procedural law and independently check the Constitution.

related.label: Rulemaking authority and choice of procedure

nodes.label: Find the governing state or local procedure
nodes.detail: The federal APA supplies no general state-agency process. Identify the state administrative procedure act, the local authority and any program-specific hearing or notice requirement, then test the federal Constitution independently.

nodes.label: Which rulemaking requirements apply?
nodes.detail: Separate APA § 553(a) exclusions from the § 553(b) exceptions for guidance, procedure and supported good cause. Check whether another statute requires notice or a hearing.

nodes.label: Identify exactly what the exception changes
nodes.detail: A § 553(b) exception addresses notice and public procedure. It does not itself resolve publication or effective-date requirements. Apply any independently required hearing or statutory procedure.

edges.label: Other law or full exclusion resolves APA procedure

nodes.label: Does the statute require an on-the-record hearing?
nodes.detail: Under § 553(c), the formal trigger concerns what the statute requires. Florida East Coast Railway found a bare hearing requirement insufficient for formal rulemaking in that context.

nodes.label: Use the formal rulemaking record
nodes.detail: Sections 556 and 557 apply in place of § 553(c). Identify separate notice and effective-date obligations. Wirtz illustrates the problem with relying on an impeached survey while withholding the underlying material.

nodes.label: Give adequate notice of the proposal
nodes.detail: Ordinarily publish in the Federal Register. Include the proceedings’ time, place and nature, the legal authority, proposed text or subjects and issues, and the § 553(b)(4) web address for a plain-language summary of up to 100 words. Named persons may receive legally adequate actual notice instead.

nodes.label: Give a meaningful opportunity to comment
nodes.detail: Allow written data, views or arguments. Nova Scotia required access to important technical material and meaningful treatment of objections. Compare the proposal and final rule for logical outgrowth.

edges.label: Comments can address the adopted approach
Final approach was not reasonably foreshadowed

nodes.label: Give renewed notice when required
nodes.detail: A material departure may require another proposal and comment opportunity so affected participants can address the new approach.

nodes.label: Explain the rule’s basis and purpose
nodes.detail: Consider relevant submissions and incorporate a concise general statement of basis and purpose under § 553(c). Boyd illustrates why the agency’s explanation must allow meaningful review.

nodes.label: Check the final rule’s effective date
nodes.detail: For substantive rules, § 553(d) generally requires publication or service at least 30 days ahead. Independently check exemptions or restrictions relieved, interpretive rules or policy statements, and good cause found and published with the rule.

nodes.label: Review the process under the governing law
nodes.detail: Vermont Yankee limits courts from adding procedures beyond applicable statute and Constitution. Courts can still test required procedure, meaningful participation and the explanation the agency gave.

nodes.label: Which adjudication statute applies?
nodes.detail: For federal adjudication, § 554 generally turns on a statute requiring on-the-record adjudication after an opportunity for agency hearing and has specified exceptions. State or local orders have their own statutory framework.

edges.label: Federal statute requires a record hearing
Statute says hearing in less specific terms

nodes.label: What does hearing mean in this statute?
nodes.detail: Marathon Oil read an opportunity for public hearing on individualized discharge permits to entail formal adjudication. Compare the text, scheme, jurisdiction and case posture. Florida East Coast Railway addressed rulemaking.

nodes.label: Use the formal adjudication process
nodes.detail: Apply §§ 554, 556 and 557 where triggered. Test notice, record evidence and fair opportunity to rebut. Perales concerns evidence, Ashbacker’s statutory hearing protects competing applicants, and Jarkesy asks separately whether a jury is required.

nodes.label: Apply the applicable informal or special procedure
nodes.detail: Identify duties in the organic statute and governing regulations, plus any otherwise applicable APA requirements. Constitutional procedure can apply even if the formal hearing provisions do not.

nodes.label: Is there a protected interest and a deprivation?
nodes.detail: Roth and Sindermann contrast a unilateral hope of renewal with a plausible entitlement based on established understandings. General policy changes typically do not require individualized hearings under Bi-Metallic. In individualized cases, test liberty or property and the deprivation separately.

edges.label: Individual deprivation of a protected interest
No individual procedural due-process claim shown

nodes.label: What procedures and timing does due process require?
nodes.detail: Mathews weighs the private interest, risk of error and value of safeguards, and government burdens. Compare the need for oral response, credibility testing, a prompt preliminary response or reliable written records.

edges.label: Reliable written record and later hearing

nodes.label: Goldberg required an evidentiary hearing before cutoff
nodes.detail: Welfare recipients faced loss of subsistence, and written submissions were inadequate for the issues the Court identified. Compare whether the case needs oral presentation and confrontation before termination.

nodes.label: Loudermill required a chance to respond before termination
nodes.detail: A for-cause employee normally gets notice of the charges, an explanation of supporting evidence and a chance to respond, followed by available post-termination procedures.

nodes.label: Mathews allowed the hearing after disability benefits ended
nodes.detail: The procedures before termination and the largely documentary medical issues reduced the value of a prior evidentiary hearing. An adequate later hearing remained available.

nodes.label: Apply the procedures supplied by governing law
nodes.detail: Where these facts do not create an individual procedural due-process right, still apply the relevant statute, regulation and state procedural law. Consider other independent constitutional limits where raised.

title: May the agency hear this claim without a jury?

nodes.label: What claim and relief are before the agency?
nodes.detail: Identify the statute, the alleged wrong, the relief requested and the forum. Jarkesy involved SEC securities fraud and civil penalties imposed in-house.

nodes.label: Does the claim nevertheless resemble a suit at common law?
nodes.detail: The Seventh Amendment analysis considers the historical analogue and the remedy. Pay particular attention to whether ostensibly equitable relief functions as legal relief.

nodes.label: Is the remedy legal in character?
nodes.detail: Jarkesy treated punitive and deterrent civil penalties as legal relief and treated securities fraud as akin to common-law fraud. Compare the statutory action with the closest historic analogue.

nodes.label: Does the claim fall within the public-rights exception?
nodes.detail: Compare historically recognized public-rights domains and the relationship to a dispute traditionally heard at law. The government’s presence or a statutory cause alone does not establish the exception.

nodes.label: Use a court and jury for the legal claim
nodes.detail: Jarkesy affirmed on the Seventh Amendment ground. The Court did not decide the Fifth Circuit’s separate nondelegation and ALJ-removal grounds.

nodes.label: Apply statutory authority and procedural requirements
nodes.detail: The Seventh Amendment analysis on this branch does not itself decide whether Congress authorized agency adjudication or supplied an agency hearing. Test independent Article III and due-process limits.

title: Who is entitled to an agency hearing, and what kind?

nodes.label: Who wants to be heard and what decision is pending?
nodes.detail: Distinguish individualized parties, participants representing public interests and competing applicants. Read the hearing language of the governing statute.

nodes.label: What hearing does the statute require?
nodes.detail: A statute requiring on-the-record adjudication after an opportunity for a hearing generally triggers § 554 and §§ 556–557, subject to statutory exceptions. Read any less explicit hearing language in its program context.

nodes.label: Can a record requirement be inferred here?
nodes.detail: Marathon Oil inferred formality in individualized discharge permitting. Florida East Coast Railway interpreted a hearing provision in rulemaking. The applicable statute and controlling jurisdiction matter.

nodes.label: Is the evidence fairly testable on the record?
nodes.detail: Perales allows qualifying medical reports to count as substantial evidence in context, where subpoena process was available. Marathon Oil rejected use of critical undisclosed extra-record material.

nodes.label: Does the participation right lose value if delayed?
nodes.detail: Ashbacker concerned both bona fide, mutually exclusive applications and an empty hearing for the loser after the rival’s grant. United Church of Christ addresses listener representation in the FCC proceeding.

nodes.label: Protect both applications before granting one
nodes.detail: Granting one mutually exclusive application can effectively deny the other. Apply the statutory hearing right before the benefit is committed.

nodes.label: Assess the public participant’s role under the statute
nodes.detail: United Church of Christ recognizes the importance of responsible listener representatives in license-renewal proceedings. Determine the kind of participation the governing statute gives this participant.

nodes.label: Provide the applicable informal process
nodes.detail: An interview, paper record, staged decision or an agency-specific hearing may fit the statute. Independently assess protected interests and the risk of error.

nodes.label: Formal process can support a decision
nodes.detail: Decide on the hearing record under the governing evidentiary standard and explain the grounds sufficiently for review.

nodes.label: Address the defect before relying on the evidence
nodes.detail: Provide a meaningful opportunity to test or answer the material as required. Marathon Oil ordered limited remand and new hearings for previously undisclosed material.

title: Is there a protected liberty or property interest?

nodes.label: What liberty or property does the claimant identify?
nodes.detail: Identify the benefit, status or freedom allegedly taken. State law, statutes, contract and settled understandings can supply an entitlement, while federal constitutional law determines what process is due.

nodes.label: Does the governing source constrain discretion?
nodes.detail: Look for a for-cause limitation, defined eligibility or settled understanding. Roth’s fixed term conferred no renewal entitlement on its facts. Perry allowed proof of de facto tenure from institutional practice.

nodes.label: What does the statute actually confer and reserve?
nodes.detail: Compare mandatory criteria and genuine discretion with the text of any entitlement disclaimer. Barry and Weston are course comparisons on benefits and the legal significance of program language.

nodes.label: Did the government impose stigma plus a change of status or right?
nodes.detail: Evaluate the publication and nature of any charge and any additional legal disability or deprivation. Roth considered charges or restrictions that could affect liberty, but found none in the university’s action.

nodes.label: What is the scope and basis of the exclusion?
nodes.detail: Cafeteria Workers concerned access to a particular sensitive workplace. Greene resolved the challenge to a broader clearance-related employment restriction on authorization grounds.

nodes.label: Determine what constitutional process is due
nodes.detail: Loudermill separated a state-created for-cause property interest from the federal constitutional minimum for termination. Apply the Mathews factors and any independent statutory procedures.

nodes.label: No protected interest shown on these facts
nodes.detail: Roth’s expectation of renewal did not suffice. Identify any statute or agency rule that separately requires a procedure.

title: What hearing is due, and when?

nodes.label: Where is the risk of erroneous deprivation?
nodes.detail: Assume a protected interest. Mathews weighs the private stake, the risk of error and value of added safeguards, and the government’s interest and burdens. Identify the moment the deprivation occurs.

edges.label: Other service, custody or urgent action

nodes.label: Does loss threaten subsistence before later review?
nodes.detail: Goldberg found a prior evidentiary hearing necessary given welfare recipients’ immediate needs and the value of oral presentation and confrontation.

nodes.label: Can written material resolve the issues reliably?
nodes.detail: Mathews involved disability decisions centered on medical records and a full later hearing. Compare retroactive relief and the cost and reliability of extending a prior oral hearing.

edges.label: Written review and later hearing suffice
Credibility is central and delay harms

nodes.label: What process is available before discharge?
nodes.detail: Loudermill required notice and an opportunity to respond to the employer’s evidence before discharge, in light of fuller post-termination review.

edges.label: Prior response plus later review fits

nodes.label: Do urgency and existing remedies change the balance?
nodes.detail: Memphis Light required notice of an opportunity to dispute billing and an opportunity to challenge it before utility termination. Brock assessed temporary reinstatement. Compare interests and available procedures in the detention materials.

edges.label: Immediate action with prompt later review fits

nodes.label: Provide meaningful process before deprivation
nodes.detail: Tailor the hearing to actual disputes, including credibility where it matters. Specify how notice, response and a decision on the record protect the interest.

nodes.label: Provide the safeguards at the stage they matter
nodes.detail: State the pre-deprivation protections and timing and adequacy of later review. Ingraham and G & G Fire Sprinklers illustrate settings in which later ordinary remedies mattered.

nodes.label: The existing process is insufficient for the tested interest
nodes.detail: Identify the omitted protection and why it would mitigate the error before repeating or reviewing the decision.

title: Can the agency make policy through this rule or order?

nodes.label: How does the agency seek to adopt this policy?
nodes.detail: Identify whether the agency wants a binding generally applicable rule, an interpretation or a precedent arising from a concrete controversy.

nodes.label: Did Congress authorize binding rules here?
nodes.detail: National Petroleum read the FTC statute before it to authorize substantive trade regulation rules. Check the statutory text, the program and any later constraints on that agency’s rulemaking procedures.

nodes.label: Will the new principle resolve the parties’ dispute?
nodes.detail: Chenery II permits policy to develop in adjudication, and Bell Aerospace recognizes agency choice in general. Wyman-Gordon’s divided opinions distinguish announcing general policy from enforcing a concrete order.

edges.label: General rule announced apart from deciding dispute

nodes.label: Would retroactive application be unfair?
nodes.detail: Compare the novelty of the rule, affected parties’ reliance, the burden of retroactivity and the statutory interests. Explain why adjudication suits the problem or whether prospective treatment is preferable.

nodes.label: Does the instrument impose new duties in operation?
nodes.detail: Check language, independent legal source, practical binding effect and staff discretion. A binding instrument calls for statutory authority and applicable legislative-rule procedure.

nodes.label: Use the authorized rulemaking route
nodes.detail: Follow the applicable APA and organic-statute procedure. Identify the contemporaneous basis for the agency’s choice and the final policy.

nodes.label: Issue a reasoned order on the dispute
nodes.detail: Identify statutory authority, explain the disposition and state how the new principle applies. Reviewing courts ordinarily consider the agency’s actual reasons.

nodes.label: Use the guidance within its legal limits
nodes.detail: An interpretation or nonbinding policy statement can guide decisions subject to the underlying statute or rule and any applicable guidance procedure.

nodes.label: The proposed form or application is unsupported
nodes.detail: Change the choice of procedure or the proposed reach if the statute allows. Separate lack of legislative authority from unfair retroactive application of a precedent.

title: What must happen before a federal rule takes effect?

nodes.label: Which statute and rulemaking stages govern?
nodes.detail: Read the organic statute and APA requirements separately. Identify any exclusion under § 553(a) and any more specific statute supplying procedure.

nodes.label: Use §§ 556–557 for the required record hearing
nodes.detail: Section 553(c) points to formal procedures where the statute requires on-the-record rulemaking after the opportunity for hearing. Wirtz concerns review of an evidentiary record and withheld survey data.

edges.label: Check independent notice and timing duties

nodes.label: Which stage does the exception cover?
nodes.detail: Section 553(a) concerns coverage of the section. Section 553(b) concerns notice and public procedure. Section 553(d) concerns how long a substantive rule waits before taking effect.

edges.label: Notice and public procedure still required
Notice or comment excused but timing applies
Specific statute or valid exclusion governs

nodes.label: Give notice with the required contents
nodes.detail: Identify the proceedings, legal authority, proposed terms or subjects and issues, and the address of the plain-language summary. Publish in the Federal Register unless the named-person actual-notice provision applies.

nodes.label: Consider relevant comments and explain the rule
nodes.detail: Provide access to important technical support where meaningful participation requires it. Consider relevant matter, address significant objections, and state the rule’s basis and purpose.

edges.label: Final approach is a logical outgrowth
Material issues were not reasonably in play

nodes.label: Renew notice and seek comment if required
nodes.detail: Use the revised proposal to let affected participants address the approach the agency is considering. Compare any independent good-cause finding on the applicable facts.

nodes.label: Publish or serve the final rule and check the date
nodes.detail: Section 553(d) ordinarily gives at least 30 days for substantive rules, subject to specified categories and good cause found and published with the rule. Also check publication and notice requirements outside § 553(d).

nodes.label: Review applies the procedures from governing law
nodes.detail: Vermont Yankee limits courts from creating extra procedural requirements. The APA, organic statute, Constitution and the agency’s explanation still supply enforceable standards.

nodes.label: Identify the consequence of the timing error
nodes.detail: Distinguish deficient notice from a premature effective date. Assess prejudice and the relief available under the applicable review statute.

title: Is the document binding law, an interpretation or a policy statement?

nodes.label: What legal effect does the document claim?
nodes.detail: Identify the existing statute or rule, the document’s language and how regulated parties and agency staff actually use it.

nodes.label: Could the agency enforce the duty without the document?
nodes.detail: Hoctor treated a specific fence-height requirement as legislative because the existing regulation supplied only a broad safety standard. National Council for Adoption similarly found added categorical duties.

nodes.label: Does the text interpret an existing legal command?
nodes.detail: An interpretive rule explains a statute or existing regulation. Perez rejected a special APA notice-and-comment requirement merely because an agency changes its prior interpretation.

nodes.label: Can officials genuinely depart from the document?
nodes.detail: Compare the case-by-case discretion in Pacific Gas with the binding effect found in Community Nutrition and General Electric. Staff practices, compliance conditions and legal consequences can matter alongside agency wording.

nodes.label: Has an interpretive rule been revised?
nodes.detail: Perez treats the APA’s interpretive-rule exception as available even for revisions. Check applicable statutory mandates, and separately ask whether the new interpretation changes underlying legal obligations.

edges.label: Revision operates as a legislative rule

nodes.label: Legislative-rule procedures govern
nodes.detail: Confirm rulemaking authority and ordinary notice and comment unless a valid exclusion or good cause applies. A label or a post hoc explanation alone cannot establish good cause.

nodes.label: The document can operate as an interpretation
nodes.detail: Its legal force depends on the underlying statute or regulation. Check any separate reviewability question against the instrument’s effects.

nodes.label: The document can operate as a general policy statement
nodes.detail: It guides the exercise of discretion and leaves room for individual decisions. Texas v. United States addressed DAPA on preliminary-injunction review and illustrates disputed claims of practical binding force.

title: Which notice-and-comment exception is actually claimed?

nodes.label: Which APA stage would the agency skip?
nodes.detail: Identify the authority the agency invoked, the document’s legal effect and the stage at issue. Check the organic statute for independent duties.

nodes.label: Does § 553(a) cover this subject?
nodes.detail: The statutory categories include military or foreign affairs functions and matters relating to specified agency operations or government property, loans, grants, benefits and contracts. Check narrower statutory obligations or a binding agency waiver.

nodes.label: Which § 553(b) ground is asserted?
nodes.detail: Check whether another statute requires notice or hearing first. Distinguish an exemption based on the nature of the rule from a good-cause finding based on the circumstances.

nodes.label: Is the document genuinely nonlegislative?
nodes.detail: An interpretation explains existing law and a policy statement leaves discretion. A practically binding instrument or a new duty can trigger ordinary procedure.

nodes.label: Does the rule actually govern agency procedure?
nodes.detail: Examine what the rule changes and the controlling circuit’s approach. A rule regulating the way parties present claims may qualify. A new substantive duty or standard raises a different question.

nodes.label: Did the agency make and publish a supported finding?
nodes.detail: The agency must incorporate its finding and brief reasons that notice and public procedure are impracticable, unnecessary or contrary to the public interest. Little Sisters considered the later final rules’ own notice-and-comment process.

nodes.label: Does § 553(d) independently require 30 days?
nodes.detail: Check whether a substantive rule grants an exemption or relieves a restriction, whether the rule is interpretive or a policy statement, or whether the agency made and published good cause specifically for timing.

nodes.label: Use ordinary notice and comment
nodes.detail: Give notice, enable meaningful participation and explain the basis and purpose. Independently calculate the effective date under § 553(d).

nodes.label: Observe the effective-date interval
nodes.detail: Satisfying a notice exception does not automatically resolve the publication-or-service timing obligation for a substantive rule.

nodes.label: Apply any remaining legal requirements
nodes.detail: Specify the ground and its procedural consequence. Check separate publication duties and any APA or organic-statute obligations that remain applicable.

title: Did the final rule receive meaningful public comment?

nodes.label: Could affected people comment on the actual approach?
nodes.detail: Compare the notice, material on which the agency relied, comments and final rule. Distinguish access to evidence from adequate notice of the issues the final rule resolves.

nodes.label: Could participants test the agency’s important technical basis?
nodes.detail: Nova Scotia found that withholding scientific material hindered meaningful comment. American Radio Relay League addressed redactions in technical studies and the resulting inability to evaluate the material.

nodes.label: Was the final approach reasonably foreseeable from the proposal?
nodes.detail: Read the proposal, alternatives and issues it put in play. In Mock, the preliminary-injunction appeal majority considered a change from a proposed concrete test to a final open-ended balancing approach.

nodes.label: Did the agency answer significant comments?
nodes.detail: Address objections that challenge key assumptions or raise material alternatives. A concise statement can be adequate if it lets participants and a court trace the agency’s reasons.

nodes.label: Can the agency rely on the tested hearing record?
nodes.detail: Wirtz addressed summary tables from withheld data, a successful attack on reliability and a failure to rehabilitate the survey. Apply the formal statute’s record and testability requirements.

edges.label: Material proof too weak or untested

nodes.label: Meaningful participation is supported
nodes.detail: Record the notice, technical materials and explanation. Other challenges, such as statutory authority or record support, remain analytically distinct.

nodes.label: Disclose or renew notice as the defect requires
nodes.detail: Release important supporting material or give fresh notice of a material change and an opportunity to comment. Independently check any properly supported exception.

nodes.label: Flag the defect for judicial review
nodes.detail: Review the notice, record and reasons the agency produced. Vermont Yankee preserves enforcement of statutory requirements while limiting additional court-imposed procedural steps.

title: Can a court review the agency’s action now?

nodes.label: What action is challenged and which review statute governs?
nodes.detail: Identify the complained-of step, plaintiff, requested relief and review channel. The APA supplies a review framework and a separate provision supplies jurisdiction. A special statute may specify where and when to petition.

nodes.label: Does § 701(a) foreclose this kind of review?
nodes.detail: Look for statutory preclusion or action committed by law to agency discretion. Evaluate the governing criteria and the particular claim. A refusal to enforce raises special presumptions.

edges.label: Claim precluded or committed to discretion

nodes.label: Is the action final and is there an adequate alternative remedy?
nodes.detail: Bennett asks whether the agency has consummated its decisionmaking and whether rights, obligations or legal consequences follow. Section 704 also addresses actions made reviewable by statute and adequate remedies in court.

edges.label: Review statute authorizes this route now
Tentative agency step or other adequate court remedy

nodes.label: Is this failure to act or a reasoned denial?
nodes.detail: Identify a withheld or delayed discrete required act, a refusal to enforce, or a denied rulemaking petition. Each draws on a different legal framework.

edges.label: Potentially reviewable discrete duty or denial

nodes.label: Is this plaintiff eligible for this relief?
nodes.detail: Test Article III standing and review authorization separately. APA § 702’s zone-of-interests analysis asks whether the plaintiff’s interest is arguably within those protected or regulated by the relevant statute.

nodes.label: Proceed to the appropriate standard of review
nodes.detail: Identify whether the case raises legal interpretation, factual support, policy discretion or required procedure. Determine what relief the review statute allows.

nodes.label: Use the proper channel or wait for a reviewable decision
nodes.detail: Failure of present reviewability may require completion of the process or use of another adequate remedy. Check any special statutory timing and route.

nodes.label: This review theory is foreclosed
nodes.detail: Identify whether the barrier is congressional preclusion or discretion with no workable legal standard. Examine other properly available claims on their own terms.

nodes.label: This plaintiff cannot maintain the claim on the stated basis
nodes.detail: Identify the missing Article III element or statutory coverage. The court’s review power and the plaintiff’s eligibility are separate inquiries.

title: Can a court compel action or review a refusal to act?

nodes.label: What did the agency fail or decline to do?
nodes.detail: Separate an unperformed duty, a decision against taking enforcement action and denial of a request to make a rule.

nodes.label: Is there a discrete action that the law requires?
nodes.detail: Norton v. SUWA limits § 706(1) to legally required discrete action. Identify a specific deadline, adjudication or required decision. A broad demand to improve program administration falls outside that framework.

nodes.label: Does the statute meaningfully constrain the refusal?
nodes.detail: Heckler v. Chaney starts with presumptive unreviewability because of resource allocation and prosecutorial judgment. Dunlop involved statutory criteria and a reviewable decision under that scheme.

nodes.label: Did the agency give the reasons required for denial?
nodes.detail: Distinguish the right to petition in § 553(e) from the obligation to explain denial in § 555(e), subject to its exceptions. Massachusetts v. EPA and Lyng test petition denials against their regulatory statutes.

edges.label: Agency has failed to act at all

nodes.label: Do the reasons address the statutory criteria?
nodes.detail: Massachusetts v. EPA rejected an explanation untethered to the governing endangerment standard. Lyng reviewed an agency’s justification for declining rulemaking on its own record.

nodes.label: A court may compel the legally required action
nodes.detail: Identify whether the action was unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed. A court may require the agency to decide while leaving lawful substantive choices to the agency.

nodes.label: This theory supplies no order compelling action
nodes.detail: Identify whether the requested act is too broad, legally discretionary, or presumptively unreviewable enforcement. Check the actual statutory grant for any different avenue.

nodes.label: The refusal can stand under this review standard
nodes.detail: The agency’s reasoned decision is evaluated against the statutory source of the duty and the type of refusal.

nodes.label: Return the decision for an agency explanation or reconsideration
nodes.detail: The court can require application of the right statutory criteria without making the agency’s policy decision for it.

title: Does the decision survive hard-look review?

nodes.label: What grounds did the agency give for the action?
nodes.detail: Collect the final explanation, the record before the agency and the statutory mandate. Review the explanation the agency actually gave.

nodes.label: Did the agency use the factors Congress prescribed?
nodes.detail: Overton Park illustrates review anchored to statute and record. Ask whether a factor was omitted or whether the agency gave weight to something Congress did not authorize.

edges.label: Material factor omitted or forbidden factor used

nodes.label: Does the record support the key premise?
nodes.detail: Trace the evidence and contrary submissions, including how the agency addressed uncertainty. In Ohio v. EPA the Court granted a stay after finding likely deficiency in the response to a significant comment about the plan’s premise.

nodes.label: Were important alternatives considered?
nodes.detail: State Farm reviewed a safety-standard rescission and faulted the agency’s treatment of options such as an airbag-only requirement. Explain the relationship of the alternative to the existing rule and statutory objectives.

nodes.label: Does the explanation fit the actual decision?
nodes.detail: Department of Commerce v. New York held the stated census rationale contrived in light of the record. Identify concrete evidence supporting the mismatch.

nodes.label: Can the court evaluate the decision on the agency’s own grounds?
nodes.detail: Chenery and Calcutt limit appellate reconstruction. A litigation explanation can clarify existing grounds but cannot ordinarily replace them with a new basis for the decision.

edges.label: Genuine contemporaneous basis can be reviewed

nodes.label: The decision clears this hard-look challenge
nodes.detail: The record and contemporary explanation reasonably connect the evidence, statutory factors and chosen action.

nodes.label: Remand for the agency to address the flaw
nodes.detail: Specify the missing statutory factor, material evidence, ignored alternative, pretext or unreviewable rationale. Assess the appropriate form of relief separately.

title: What must an agency explain when it changes policy?

nodes.label: Is the agency adopting a position for the first time or reversing course?
nodes.detail: Identify the prior policy, the new decision and the statutory factors governing both. Fox distinguishes ordinary reasoned explanation from situations requiring explanation for special consequences of a change.

nodes.label: Are the first decision’s reasons adequate?
nodes.detail: Identify the action’s statutory basis, significant evidence and alternatives. The required explanation depends on the material issues the record presents.

nodes.label: Has the agency acknowledged the change?
nodes.detail: The agency should display awareness that it is changing course and explain why the new position is permissible and preferable in its judgment. Fox did not impose a universal heightened standard.

nodes.label: Does the new rule contradict earlier factual findings?
nodes.detail: Identify earlier findings underlying the policy and the record for the new view. Explain any factual departure in light of the evidence.

nodes.label: Did people seriously rely, and are alternatives available?
nodes.detail: Regents required consideration of important reliance interests and whether forbearance could be separated from benefits. Explain how the agency assessed reliance and feasible alternatives.

nodes.label: The agency supplied a reasoned policy explanation
nodes.detail: Record what changed and why, and what the agency concluded about prior findings, legitimate reliance and alternatives where they matter.

nodes.label: Reconsider the change on a reasoned record
nodes.detail: The agency can make a different choice after considering the required factors. Use the agency’s contemporaneous explanation to evaluate the revised decision.

title: How should a court review a factual or scientific determination?

nodes.label: What part of the decision is disputed?
nodes.detail: Separate the statute’s meaning, factfinding, application of law to fact, and technical or policy judgment. Read the particular review statute and identify the agency procedure used.

nodes.label: Does the dispute concern the legal standard or its application?
nodes.detail: Interpret the statute independently. For mixed questions, identify the legal standard and the factual finding supporting its application. Dickinson v. Zurko rejected a special clear-error approach to Patent Office factual findings.

nodes.label: Is the evidence substantial on the record as a whole?
nodes.detail: Universal Camera requires consideration of contrary evidence and the hearing examiner’s findings. Biestek rejects a categorical rule about withheld vocational data and considers context.

nodes.label: How well supported is the technical or predictive judgment?
nodes.detail: Benzene’s assigned notes distinguish the legal requirement of significant risk from uncertain dose-response evidence. Examine assumptions, extrapolation, uncertainty and the reasons for the policy choice.

edges.label: Review of factual support remains disputed

nodes.label: Which review provision and record apply?
nodes.detail: ADAPSO treated arbitrary-and-capricious and substantial-evidence review as requiring the same quantum of factual support while distinguishing records. Safe Extensions reviewed material the FAA actually had in informal adjudication.

edges.label: Record supports the finding under governing test

nodes.label: Resolve the legal issue independently
nodes.detail: State the statutory requirement and review separately whatever factual and discretionary judgments the law leaves the agency.

nodes.label: Sustain the supported factual determination
nodes.detail: Identify the evidence, the important contrary material and the role of any scientific or policy uncertainty under the proper standard.

nodes.label: Return unsupported findings for agency consideration
nodes.detail: Identify what the record fails to show. Do not replace the agency’s finding with the court’s own technical or evidentiary judgment where the agency must decide.

title: What remedy follows an agency error?

nodes.label: What did the court find unlawful, and what relief is requested?
nodes.detail: Read the review statute and match the remedy to the defect, the requested relief and the affected parties. The assigned standing excerpt introduces the distinction between APA setting aside and injunctions and ends before resolving the broader debate.

nodes.label: Can the agency lawfully make the remaining judgment?
nodes.detail: Calcutt applies the ordinary remand rule where an agency decision cannot stand on its stated grounds. Identify whether substantive judgment or evidence still belongs to the agency.

nodes.label: Could the action remain in place while the agency reconsiders?
nodes.detail: Under the course’s Allied-Signal account, evaluate the seriousness of the deficiency and disruptive consequences of immediate vacatur. Check the jurisdiction’s approach and the statutory limits on that choice.

nodes.label: Which form and scope of relief fit the defect?
nodes.detail: APA § 706 addresses setting aside unlawful agency action. An injunction orders a party to act or refrain and has separate equitable and scope requirements. Identify the source for each requested remedy.

edges.label: Set aside and remand is available

nodes.label: Set the action aside and return it to the agency where warranted
nodes.detail: Specify the unlawful action and the scope of the judgment. Assess a request for an additional injunction separately.

nodes.label: Remand without vacatur where the governing law allows it
nodes.detail: The challenged action remains operative during reconsideration. The course’s Core Communications example shows how a deadline backed by vacatur can address prolonged delay.

nodes.label: Apply the injunction standard and determine lawful scope
nodes.detail: Identify harm and the scope needed to give the parties complete relief. In Trump v. CASA, the Court partially stayed universal preliminary injunctions and reserved the question of APA vacatur.

nodes.label: Declare the parties’ legal rights where the remedy is available
nodes.detail: A declaratory judgment answers a live legal controversy. Its practical consequences and any further order require separate analysis.

title: Who interprets an agency-administered statute after Loper Bright?

nodes.label: What kind of determination did the agency make?
nodes.detail: Loper Bright overruled Chevron on June 28, 2024. Identify whether the controversy concerns statutory meaning, actual delegated discretion, a regulation’s meaning or record facts.

nodes.label: What is the statute’s best reading?
nodes.detail: Use ordinary interpretive tools in independent judicial judgment. Statutory ambiguity alone supplies no duty to accept the agency’s reasonable reading.

edges.label: Court identifies an actual grant of discretion
No delegation or persuasive agency view

nodes.label: How much persuasive weight has the agency earned?
nodes.detail: Skidmore considers thoroughness, reasoning, consistency and other sources of persuasive power. Specialized experience and contemporaneous understanding can inform independent judgment.

nodes.label: What bounds and criteria did Congress supply?
nodes.detail: The court independently identifies the delegation’s boundaries. An express or contextually identifiable grant can let the agency fill details or exercise bounded judgment. Review how it acted within that authority.

nodes.label: Does an earlier holding govern the same issue?
nodes.detail: Loper Bright states that final holdings on specific agency actions remain subject to statutory stare decisis. Reliance on Chevron alone does not supply a special justification to overrule those holdings.

nodes.label: Use the standard for this distinct question
nodes.detail: Interpretation of the agency’s rule invokes the Kisor analysis where appropriate. Evidentiary disputes take the standard assigned by the governing review statute.

nodes.label: Apply the independently determined statutory meaning
nodes.detail: State the court’s reading and whether the agency stayed within statutory limits. Address the persuasiveness of its interpretation if it mattered.

nodes.label: Review the authorized exercise of discretion
nodes.detail: Where Congress committed a choice to the agency, enforce the delegation’s boundaries and use the appropriate record and reasoned-decisionmaking review.

nodes.label: Apply the relevant statutory precedent
nodes.detail: Identify the holding and jurisdiction. Address ordinary stare decisis before deciding whether the precedential result applies to the new dispute.

title: How did judicial treatment of agency interpretation change?

nodes.label: Which period or kind of authority is under study?
nodes.detail: The course compares several approaches to legal and mixed questions. Choose historical practice, the Chevron era, empirical research or post-2024 doctrine.

nodes.label: Compare the questions in Gray, Hearst and Skidmore
nodes.detail: Gray and Hearst gave weight to agency decisions applying statutory categories. Skidmore accorded an interpretation persuasive weight depending on its merits. The assigned pre-APA history remains contested.

nodes.label: Did the historical Chevron framework apply?
nodes.detail: Chevron first tested whether Congress had directly answered the question. If a gap or ambiguity remained under that regime, courts asked whether the agency’s construction was permissible.

edges.label: Check the gatekeeping and precedent cases

nodes.label: How did Mead and Brand X qualify the old framework?
nodes.detail: Mead looked to congressional authority to make force-of-law rules and whether the interpretation exercised it. Brand X generally let a qualifying later agency interpretation displace a judicial reading that had left ambiguity.

nodes.label: Which court, years and denominator did the study use?
nodes.detail: The assigned Supreme Court study examined the 1983–2005 Terms and found express Chevron use in 8.3% of its 1,014-case sample. Circuit research for 2003–2013 asked different questions about lower-court use and outcomes.

nodes.label: What changed on June 28, 2024?
nodes.detail: Loper Bright requires independent judicial interpretation and preserves actual statutory delegations. Skidmore’s persuasive considerations can inform that judgment and earlier holdings remain subject to stare decisis.

nodes.label: Record the result under the historical test
nodes.detail: Distinguish a pre-2024 holding from the method used to reach it. Chevron no longer supplies a rule of statutory deference.

nodes.label: Compare only what the assigned datasets measured
nodes.detail: Case selection, denominator, court level, time and outcome definition affect the comparison. The studies cited here address historical periods.

nodes.label: Apply independent judgment and review delegated choices separately
nodes.detail: The court decides statutory meaning. When it identifies actual delegated discretion, it polices statutory bounds and applies the relevant review standard to the agency’s exercise of discretion.

title: Does Kisor apply to the agency’s reading of its own rule?

nodes.label: Is this the agency’s interpretation of its own rule?
nodes.detail: Kisor concerns regulatory interpretation, while Loper Bright governs an agency’s interpretation of a statute. Identify precisely which text produced the dispute.

nodes.label: Does genuine ambiguity remain after ordinary tools?
nodes.detail: Exhaust text, structure, history and purpose. Kisor rejected automatic reliance on ambiguity and remanded the veterans-benefits case for application of the proper approach.

nodes.label: Does the agency reading fit the permissible range?
nodes.detail: Genuine ambiguity leaves boundaries. Compare the agency’s interpretation with the permissible readings left after using ordinary tools.

nodes.label: Does the position reflect agency authority and expertise?
nodes.detail: Look for an authoritative position attributable to the agency and relevant substantive expertise. An ad hoc view outside the agency’s expertise carries a different status.

nodes.label: Is this the agency’s fair and considered judgment?
nodes.detail: Examine consistent treatment, reliance, unfair surprise and any convenience or post hoc litigation rationale. The circumstances must justify giving the reading controlling weight.

nodes.label: The qualifying interpretation can receive controlling weight
nodes.detail: State the genuine ambiguity and why the agency’s position is reasonable and qualifies under Kisor’s character-and-context requirements.

nodes.label: Resolve the regulatory meaning without Kisor deference
nodes.detail: Use the court’s own reading. Consider persuasive reasoning on its merits where appropriate.

nodes.label: Use the framework governing the actual text
nodes.detail: For an agency’s reading of a statute, use independent judgment and identify any genuine delegation of discretion under Loper Bright.

title: Does the asserted power present a major question?

nodes.label: How unusual is the authority the agency asserts?
nodes.detail: Specify the regulated parties and practical scale, novelty, economic or political significance, and the fit with the agency’s usual statutory role.

edges.label: Broad power claimed under an older provision
Question about delegation or statutory interpretation

nodes.label: Which part of the statute supplies the asserted authority?
nodes.detail: West Virginia’s 2022 merits decision found no clear authorization for electricity generation shifting under the provision invoked. Biden v. Nebraska’s 2023 merits decision rejected the asserted basis for the large debt-cancellation program.

nodes.label: What showing did the Court decide provisionally?
nodes.detail: NFIB v. OSHA stayed the broad workplace rule. Biden v. Missouri stayed injunctions against conditions on participating health facilities. Alabama Realtors vacated a stay keeping the eviction moratorium operative. Compare the statutory powers and stay posture.

edges.label: Broad power from an unexpected source

nodes.label: Is the question the statute’s reach or delegation’s validity?
nodes.detail: King v. Burwell resolved the tax-credit question itself based on statutory context, declining Chevron’s historical approach. Benzene’s plurality construed a threshold risk finding. The REINS material concerns an institutional proposal.

edges.label: Question concerns validity of the delegation

nodes.label: Can the agency point to clear congressional authorization?
nodes.detail: Read the specific language and the full statutory scheme. Novel breadth, mismatched agency expertise or reliance on a longstanding ancillary provision can sharpen the inquiry.

nodes.label: Resolve statutory authority and any remaining challenge
nodes.detail: If the agency’s authority fits the statute, test the exercise of that power and applicable procedure. A stay ruling expresses a decision at the preliminary stage.

nodes.label: The asserted power falls outside the statutory grant
