nodes.detail: Identify the power the opinion rejects and whether its reasoning was applied at a stay stage or in a final merits disposition.

nodes.label: Examine Congress’s enactment under the delegation framework
nodes.detail: Ask who made the policy and what instructions and limits Congress supplied. The major-questions inquiry asks whether Congress granted the claimed authority.

title: Does this plaintiff have standing to obtain the requested relief?

nodes.label: Who claims injury and what relief does that person seek?
nodes.detail: Article III standing requires injury, traceability and redressability for the plaintiff, claim and relief. Match the showing to the procedural stage.

nodes.label: Is harm concrete, particularized and actual or imminent?
nodes.detail: Sierra Club’s interest in conservation did not identify injury to it or its members. Spokeo distinguished concrete harm from a bare procedural violation. For prospective relief examine the risk of future harm.

nodes.label: Is a concrete interest affected by the right at issue?
nodes.detail: Lujan links procedural standing to a concrete interest, with some relaxation of ordinary immediacy and redressability requirements. Havens recognizes an injury to a tester denied truthful information Congress entitled her to receive.

edges.label: Only a bare violation or undifferentiated objection

nodes.label: Can the plaintiff identify a differentiated interest?
nodes.detail: Generalized dissatisfaction with government compliance or a diffuse institutional objection ordinarily falls short. Raines distinguishes legislators’ asserted institutional injury from a personal legal injury.

nodes.label: Is harm fairly traceable to this defendant’s action?
nodes.detail: Map the actual causal links, including third parties. California v. Texas illustrates the difficulty of attributing costs to an unenforced statutory requirement.

nodes.label: Would the requested order likely redress this injury?
nodes.detail: Identify what the court can order and how it affects the plaintiff. United States v. Texas also illustrates the historical limit on suits seeking more enforcement against other people.

nodes.label: Article III standing is established for this relief
nodes.detail: Test the applicable cause of action and statutory access to APA review independently.

nodes.label: Standing fails at the identified element
nodes.detail: Identify the missing fact or inference and the procedural posture. A failure of Article III standing prevents merits adjudication of this claim.

title: Does this plaintiff fall within the statute’s protected interests?

nodes.label: Which question about this plaintiff is at issue?
nodes.detail: Distinguish Article III injury and the statute’s cause of action. Section 702 authorizes APA review for eligible plaintiffs, with zone of interests tested against the relevant statute.

nodes.label: Does the plaintiff identify concrete Article III harm?
nodes.detail: Akins considered impairment of access to information a statute required to be disclosed. Compare whether the asserted harm corresponds to the statutory right and separately test traceability and redressability.

nodes.label: Which statutory provision and interest matter?
nodes.detail: Identify the substantive statute whose violation is alleged. ADAPSO and NCUA recognized competitors within the relevant zone. The APA standard is generally generous to arguably protected or regulated interests.

edges.label: The interest is plausibly protected or regulated

nodes.label: How closely is this interest related to the program?
nodes.detail: Air Courier treated postal employees’ job interests as outside the relevant provision’s zone. Patchak found a nearby landowner’s interests plausibly within the statute’s relevant concerns. Describe the plaintiff’s interest at the level matching the provision.

nodes.label: Who did this statute authorize to sue?
nodes.detail: Apply the specific cause of action. Bennett compared broad citizen-suit language and the distinct APA route. Thompson and Newport News show the significance of different statutory language and context.

nodes.label: The identified statutory avenue is available to this plaintiff
nodes.detail: Complete other reviewability requirements. Statutory authorization and Article III remain separate conditions.

nodes.label: The identified statute supplies this plaintiff no cause of action
nodes.detail: Specify which grant or relevant interests rule out this plaintiff. An Article III injury can coexist with failure under this statute.

nodes.label: Article III prevents merits review
nodes.detail: Identify the missing constitutional element even if the statute grants a substantive or procedural right.

title: Can an association, third party or state bring this challenge?

nodes.label: Whose legal injury or right supplies the claim?
nodes.detail: A member, an organization, an injured representative or a state can invoke different theories. Identify the claimant and the requested remedy before applying the standing test.

nodes.label: Do identified members have standing in their own right?
nodes.detail: Apply the standing elements to an injured member. The interests must be germane to the association’s purpose. Brock illustrates organizational litigation on members’ behalf.

nodes.label: Would the claim or relief require individual participation?
nodes.detail: Compare common prospective relief and individualized proof. Brown Group treated the participation requirement as prudential and recognized that Congress can displace it in an appropriate statute.

edges.label: Participation unnecessary or statute appropriately displaces requirement

nodes.label: Did the organization itself suffer a concrete injury?
nodes.detail: Ordinary spending to oppose a policy is insufficient by itself. In Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine, the Court separated lobbying-related costs from the practical interference identified in Havens.

edges.label: Direct concrete injury traceable and redressable

links.label: FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine

nodes.label: Does an injured litigant have the right relationship and justification?
nodes.detail: Ordinarily ask whether the litigant is injured, has a close relationship with the right-holder, and whether the right-holder faces a hindrance to vindicating the right independently.

nodes.label: What state interest and statutory right support standing?
nodes.detail: In Massachusetts v. EPA, statutory procedure and threatened state-owned land mattered to special solicitude. United States v. Texas rejected standing to demand more third-party enforcement. Separate holdings from competing scholarship.

edges.label: State's theory satisfies the applicable conditions
Sovereign label supplies no adequate basis

nodes.label: Proceed on the established representation or injury theory
nodes.detail: Identify the injuries supporting standing, who is represented, and the remedy that can address the harm. Apply any independent statutory review requirements.

nodes.label: This standing or representation theory fails
nodes.detail: Identify exactly which claimant or requirement is missing. Another eligible plaintiff or a properly supported direct claim could present a distinct theory.

title: Can a federal court still resolve this dispute?

nodes.label: Did the case lose a live dispute, or present a nonjusticiable question?
nodes.detail: Mootness concerns continued personal stake in relief. Political question doctrine concerns the justiciability of a particular issue at all.

edges.label: Later event may have ended the controversy
Issue claimed to be politically committed

nodes.label: Can the court still give effective relief?
nodes.detail: Assess the requested remedies and subsequent events. In Laidlaw, civil penalties payable to the government could still redress the injuries by deterring future violations.

nodes.label: Has the defendant shown recurrence cannot reasonably be expected?
nodes.detail: Laidlaw puts a heavy burden on the party claiming mootness after voluntary cessation. Identify the conduct, evidence of recurrence risk and remaining remedial effects.

edges.label: Burden not met or redress remains

nodes.label: Does a recognized basis preserve justiciability?
nodes.detail: For capable of repetition yet evading review, check short duration and whether the same complaining party can reasonably expect recurrence. Also consider any continuing consequences or proper class context.

nodes.label: Are there legal standards a federal court can administer?
nodes.detail: Rucho’s majority found no manageable federal standard for adjudicating partisan gerrymandering. The dissent identified standards it believed courts could apply. Distinguish political salience from constitutional commitment or absence of standards.

nodes.label: The case can proceed past this justiciability inquiry
nodes.detail: Record the live relief or the available legal standard. Apply the remaining jurisdictional and merits elements independently.

nodes.label: The dispute is moot
nodes.detail: Identify the later event and why the court can no longer grant effective relief. Address the proper appellate disposition if a judgment is already on review.

nodes.label: The federal court cannot decide this issue on the merits
nodes.detail: Rucho rejected federal constitutional partisan-gerrymandering claims as political questions. Its reasoning does not resolve separate claims governed by distinct legal standards.

title: When does a problem call for administrative regulation?

nodes.label: Is there a problem that warrants public intervention?
nodes.detail: Class 2, Introduction to Regulation and the Administrative State, slides 23 and 26–30. Use the algal-bloom example to identify the harm, its causes and who bears it. These notes follow the slide deck. The linked atlas entries provide related course context.

edges.label: Material harm or public objective identified
No public problem or objective is shown

nodes.label: Could private law make the harm manageable?
nodes.detail: Slides 24–25 compare bargaining among affected parties with tort claims. Ask whether claimants can organize, identify sources and prove causation, and whether a remedy after harm gives enough incentive to prevent it.

nodes.label: What justifies public regulation, and who would bear its burdens?
nodes.detail: Slides 26–28 ask whether regulation is justified. Count costs imposed on downstream communities, information gaps and public benefits. Also consider equality, duties to future generations and values independent of price. Weigh the burdens, who pays, effects on entry or innovation, and the fairness of the procedure. The political reasons a measure might pass answer a different question.

edges.label: The case for a public response is insufficient

nodes.label: Can the legislature write the conduct rule itself?
nodes.detail: Slides 29–30 distinguish choosing a public goal from deciding who should administer it. Ask whether lawmakers can set the rule directly or whether the program needs ongoing factfinding, technical detail or case-by-case decisions.

edges.label: A direct legal standard is enough

nodes.label: What responsibility and discretion would the agency need?
nodes.detail: Slide 30 asks whether to put an agency in charge before choosing its tools. For recurring water-quality problems, compare the need to collect data, update standards and resolve particular applications, and specify what decisions the legislature would keep.

edges.label: Direct legislation can achieve the objective

nodes.label: Which tool addresses the problem identified?
nodes.detail: Slide 30 leaves tool selection open. In the algal-bloom example, compare monitoring or disclosure for information gaps, standards for diffuse risks and individual permits where source-specific decisions matter. Choose authority, a decisionmaker and a reviewable legal standard.

nodes.label: Use private bargaining or legal remedies
nodes.detail: Slides 24–25 ask whether contracts and tort recovery could reach the parties responsible and mitigate the harm. Explain how transactions or litigation would change incentives in the example.

nodes.label: The record does not yet justify a public response
nodes.detail: Slides 26–28 ask for the normative case on both sides. Identify which expected benefits, distributional effects or proof of harm could alter that conclusion.

nodes.label: Legislature prescribes the relevant conduct
nodes.detail: Slides 29–30 separate direct legislative prescriptions from rules that need ongoing agency implementation. Identify how the statute can be enforced and what questions, if any, remain for an agency.

nodes.label: Delegate bounded rulemaking authority
nodes.detail: Slide 30 asks what tools the agency should have. Specify the public goal, authorized standards and procedure. In the course’s later framework, test the grant and the rulemaking process independently.

nodes.label: Choose an individualized decision process
nodes.detail: Slide 30 asks what tools the agency should have. Identify the statutory criteria for the order, who may participate and the legal consequence. Connect to the later course discussion of adjudication and procedural safeguards.

nodes.label: Use information requirements fitted to the objective
nodes.detail: Slides 26 and 30 connect justification and tool choice. Identify who knows the relevant facts, what information would change behavior and whether the resulting costs fall where the legislature intends.

title: One forum clause in two courses

nodes.label: A cruise ticket selects Florida. What is disputed?
nodes.detail: Carnival Cruise enforced the clause in federal admiralty after the passengers conceded notice. A new dispute may raise formation, forum fairness, jurisdiction or the mechanism for enforcing the clause.

edges.label: Did the customer agree to it?
What does a valid clause do?

nodes.label: When and how did the term appear?
nodes.detail: Read the purchase process, ticket presentation and opportunities to reject. Specht found that an inconspicuous webpage link failed to supply sufficient notice. Hill and Klocek took different approaches to later-shipped terms.

edges.label: No sufficient notice or manifestation of assent

nodes.label: Is the forum term fundamentally fair under the governing law?
nodes.detail: Carnival rejected a categorical bargaining requirement. Its admiralty inquiry examined the clause’s commercial rationale, fraud or overreaching and serious inconvenience. Determine the applicable contract regime in the new case.

nodes.label: Which claims and courts does the clause cover?
nodes.detail: Read the actual language. A forum clause may give consent to personal jurisdiction or require suit in a designated place. Check whether it makes that forum exclusive and whether it reaches the pending claim.

edges.label: Exclusive and applies to this claim

nodes.label: Is the selected forum another federal court?
nodes.detail: Atlantic Marine assumes a valid clause. Statutory venue in the original forum can be proper even if that forum is different from the one the parties selected.

edges.label: Federal forum selected and original venue proper

nodes.label: Analyze transfer under § 1404(a)
nodes.detail: Atlantic Marine excludes the usual private-interest objections, removes weight from the plaintiff’s forum choice and uses transferee choice-of-law rules on the facts it addresses. Exceptional public-interest factors can still matter.

nodes.label: Analyze dismissal through forum non conveniens
nodes.detail: When the selected forum is outside the federal transfer system, use the forum non conveniens mechanism and the rule applicable to an enforceable clause.

nodes.label: Use ordinary forum rules where the clause does not control
nodes.detail: Consent in a permissive clause may still affect personal jurisdiction. Determine statutory venue and the applicable transfer or dismissal route on their own terms.

nodes.label: Continue without enforcing this term
nodes.detail: If formation or a valid defense defeats the clause, evaluate personal jurisdiction and venue independently.

title: One hearing problem in civil litigation and agency action

nodes.label: What deprivation is proposed, and who initiates it?
nodes.detail: Both routes weigh error and timing. In civil litigation the state can act at a private plaintiff’s request. In administration the agency makes an eligibility or benefit decision.

nodes.label: What happens to the defendant’s property before judgment?
nodes.detail: Doehr involved an ex parte attachment restricting use of a home where the plaintiff bringing the tort claim had no existing interest in the home. Fuentes and Sniadach provide other examples of pre-hearing interference.

nodes.label: What protects against error on the plaintiff’s claim?
nodes.detail: Under Doehr’s modified Mathews analysis, compare the debtor’s interest, evidentiary risk and value of safeguards, and the plaintiff’s interest and any government burden. Assess exigency, sworn proof, review, notice and hearing.

edges.label: Urgency and safeguards support different timing

nodes.label: Does the recipient have a protected entitlement?
nodes.detail: Identify the source and nature of the entitlement and the deprivation. Notice, termination timing and the value of additional safeguards depend on the facts.

nodes.label: What does the benefit decision depend on?
nodes.detail: Goldberg found immediate subsistence and the need to test disputed facts supported a pretermination hearing. Mathews found the disability decision’s largely documentary record and later hearing supported different timing.

edges.label: Subsistence or disputed credibility requires a prior hearing
Reliable pre-deprivation steps and effective later review

nodes.label: Provide meaningful process before the deprivation
nodes.detail: Specify what must be tested and why waiting would cause harm. The claimant’s participation and the required form of hearing depend on the context.

nodes.label: Identify justified early and later safeguards
nodes.detail: Record the circumstances supporting action before a full hearing. State what notice, preliminary response and prompt later review can reduce error, and whether relief can repair the harm.

nodes.label: Identify another procedural source where applicable
nodes.detail: Check the applicable state statute, court procedure or program rules when the facts do not establish the asserted constitutional deprivation.

title: What legal work does reliance do here?

nodes.label: Whose conduct changed in reliance on what?
nodes.detail: A promise can induce a change of position. A public agency’s established policy can also induce reliance, which can become relevant to the reasons required for changing that policy.

edges.label: A promise induced action or forbearance

nodes.label: Did the promise reasonably and foreseeably induce a concrete change?
nodes.detail: Feinberg retired because of a pension assurance. Ask what the promisor should have expected and what the promisee actually did or refrained from doing.

nodes.label: What loss should enforcement address?
nodes.detail: D & G Stout distinguished the lost benefit of a forgone sale opportunity from anticipated profits on a terminable distributorship. Section 90 permits relief limited as justice requires.

nodes.label: Did the policy create serious reliance interests?
nodes.detail: Fox addresses the need for explanation where a prior policy induced serious reliance. Regents considered people who organized important personal and professional decisions around DACA.

nodes.label: Did the agency assess reliance and available alternatives?
nodes.detail: An agency can change policy after considering important reliance. Regents found the rescission explanation inadequate, including treatment of reliance and the possibility of separating forbearance from benefits.

nodes.label: The promise can be enforceable on a reliance theory
nodes.detail: Fit the extent of enforcement and any award to the promise, induced act and applicable remedial limits.

nodes.label: Promissory estoppel fails on the stated facts
nodes.detail: Specify whether the promise, inducement, reasonable reliance or need to avoid injustice is missing. An independent bargain claim has different requirements.

nodes.label: Assess the agency’s reasons for changing course
nodes.detail: Check acknowledgment of the change, statutory factors and record support. Consideration of reliance forms part of that review where reliance is material.

nodes.label: Return the policy change for reasoned agency consideration
nodes.detail: The court reviews the agency’s decision process and can require reconsideration. The agency can reach a lawful policy decision after giving the required explanation.

title: Who gets to supply the meaning of a legal text?

nodes.label: Who made the text, and what is the reader being asked to decide?
nodes.detail: Parties make a contract and a legislature enacts a statute. Identify the disputed document, decisionmaker and whether the question concerns a missing term or the meaning of existing words.

nodes.label: Is the evidence offered to add a term or interpret a term?
nodes.detail: Check integration and contradiction when a party offers an earlier agreement. Masterson allowed evidence of a limitation on assignment because the deed was not necessarily the complete agreement.

nodes.label: Does the governing parol-evidence rule allow it for this purpose?
nodes.detail: Distinguish complete and partial integration and any applicable exception. Different approaches to integration help explain the difference between Masterson and Gianni.

nodes.label: Which interpretive approach governs?
nodes.detail: W.W.W. Associates illustrates New York’s text-first approach. Pacific Gas asks whether language is reasonably susceptible to the proposed meaning. For sales, Nanakuli shows how trade usage can qualify a posted-price term.

nodes.label: What meaning can the enacted text and its context bear?
nodes.detail: Begin with ordinary or technical meaning, statutory structure and surrounding provisions. Katzmann contrasts textualist and purposivist accounts of which materials help explain publicly enacted legal language.

edges.label: Legislative material or canon bears on the dispute

nodes.label: What inference does the source support?
nodes.detail: For legislative history, identify the producer, timing and relationship to the enacted text. For a canon, identify the textual feature and any counter-reading. Holy Trinity used evidence of statutory purpose.

edges.label: Weigh the evidence under the applicable method

nodes.label: Use the integrated agreement for the point at issue
nodes.detail: The excluded prior agreement cannot change the integrated terms. Evidence offered to interpret those terms or prove a distinct defense needs the governing rule for that purpose.

nodes.label: Determine the parties’ enforceable agreement
nodes.detail: Explain which materials the court can consider and which reasonable reading they support. The jurisdiction and commercial context determine the contract-specific inquiry.

nodes.label: Determine the enacted provision’s legal meaning
nodes.detail: Explain the reading supported by the public text and the sources the method treats as relevant. Specify how the reading fits the statute as a whole.
